transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… my eating has been kind of off for a while. Some nights I just skip dinner and I’ve lost some weight without really trying. Other nights I’ll just pick at crackers or cereal because cooking for just me feels… pointless. It’s been going on for months, and I figured I should probably come in.
Have you ever eaten a large amount of food in a short period of time, feeling like you couldn't stop?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I might snack here and there, but not like a large amount where I couldn’t stop.
Are you worried about gaining weight?
Not really… no. I don’t think that’s what this is about.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in food in general?

Yeah… kind of. It’s not that I hate food or anything, I just don’t really feel like dealing with it. Some nights I skip dinner, or I’ll just have crackers or cereal because cooking for myself feels pointless. It’s been like that for months.
Do you think your weight or body shape has anything to do with how you've been eating lately?

No… I don’t think it’s about my weight or how I look. It’s more that my appetite’s been off for months. Sometimes I just skip dinner and lose weight without meaning to, and other nights I’ll just pick at crackers or cereal because cooking feels… pointless.
Have you been feeling sad, empty, or hopeless lately?
I don’t know… maybe a little. I wouldn’t say it in big terms, but things have felt pretty flat lately.
Have you been feeling sad most of the day?
I’m not sure I’d say most of the day. It comes and goes… mostly things just feel kind of muted.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over these months?
Some, yeah. I haven’t been trying to. My appetite just… goes off, and I’ll skip dinner for stretches. I’ve noticed my weight going down during those times.
Have you noticed a decrease in enjoyment from activities you used to find pleasurable?
Yeah… a bit. I still do things, like water the garden or go to book club, but it doesn’t really feel the same. A lot of the time it’s just kind of flat, and I’ll leave early or not bother starting.
Do you feel like you've been sad more often than not over the past few months?
I don’t know… maybe not “sad” exactly. It’s more like I’ve just been kind of low or dulled out, off and on. I wouldn’t say I’m crying all the time or anything.
Have you had trouble sleeping lately?

Yeah… some. I can fall asleep okay most nights, but I’ve been waking up really early, around four. Then my mind starts going over bills or work things… the divorce. I don’t really get back to sleep after that.
Have you had thoughts of death or suicide lately?

I… I don’t have a plan to hurt myself. But sometimes I do catch myself thinking it might be a relief not to wake up. And that scares me, honestly… because if a client said that to me, I’d take it seriously.
Have you felt a lack of energy or fatigue most days over the past few months?

Yeah… I guess so. Even when work isn’t that bad, I feel like I’m sort of dragging myself through the day at the hospital. By the time I get home, I’m too wiped out to cook or stretch or even answer texts.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things most of the time?
Yeah… I think so. I still do things, like water the garden or go to book club sometimes, but it doesn’t really feel like much. I’ll leave early, or I just don’t start. It’s kind of… flat.
Do you think your lack of interest in food is connected to your feelings of being low or dulled out?

Probably, yeah. My appetite’s been… not normal for months. Some nights I just skip dinner and don’t really care, and I’ve lost some weight without trying. Other nights I’ll just pick at cereal or crackers because cooking for myself feels… pointless, I guess.
Do you think your feelings of being low or dulled out started before or after your eating habits changed?

I think the low feeling was there first… or at least around the same time. The eating part is what finally made me come in, though. My appetite’s been all over the place for months—some nights I skip dinner, and other nights it’s just crackers or cereal because cooking feels pointless.
Have you had at least two weeks where you felt low or dulled out most of the day?
Yeah. More than two weeks. It’s been… since the divorce was finalized, really. About a year and seven months now.
Have you felt low or dulled out nearly every day since the divorce was finalized?
Yeah… pretty much. It’s been there since then, about a year and seven months.
Have you felt low or dulled out for most of every day for at least two weeks at any point since the divorce?
Yes… that’s been going on since the divorce was finalized. About a year and seven months ago.
